newsitem.title: HUNGARY: FORECAST - Hungary govt paper yields might go up.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Hungary govt paper yields might go up.

text.p: The decline of Hungarian state security yields on the secondary market is likely to slow down this week, or even slight upwards correction might come, dealers said on Monday.
"The pace of fall will obviously slow down (compared with last week)," said Gyula Kerdo of Creditanstalt.
"Perhaps a small correction will come, but it's a pessimistic forecast," said ING Barings' Akos Bereznai.
The yields changed little between Monday and Thursday last week, but they fell some 0.3 percentage points following the auction of the government bonds of 1998/K series on Thursday. @
"The yields dropped last week, and it was clearly after the auction of the 1998/K," said Kerdo.

The yield of the 1998/K bonds dropped to 21.99 percent on strong demand triggered by expectations of the decline of inflation and interest rates, at last week's auction from 22.85 set at an auction two weeks before.

The yield of two-year papers was around 22.3 percent on the secondary market last week, one-year and six-month yields were at around 22.6 percent and the yields on one- and three-month Treasury bills stood at levels between 22.3 and 22.4 percent. @
The Government Debt Management Agency's plans of issues for this year showed that it would sell less securities than buying capacities on the market, dealers said.
But many investors may take up a wait and see attitude this week, as the yields have dropped very sharply recently.
"Larger investors will wait, they will not buy at these levels," said Andrea Veres of Postabank Securities.

However, yields may drop further by 0.1 to 0.2 percentage points this week, when the yield to be set at the auction of 12-month Treasury bills on Friday is likely to mark the direction, dealers said. @
